title: standardize(api): unify rate-limit semantics, idempotency handling, Retry-After and OpenAI-compat error shape
author: Claire Nguyen
description:
Motivation: Customers and SDKs reported inconsistent rate-limit headers and error bodies across streaming and non-streaming endpoints which caused clients (including OpenAI-compatible SDKs) to mis-handle backoff and idempotent retries. This PR unifies rate-limit semantics and idempotency behavior across the Redwood API surface and the OpenAI compatibility layer.

Summary of changes: standardize 429 responses to always include Retry-After in seconds where applicable; expose consistent rate-limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset) for both streaming and non-streaming endpoints; ensure streaming payloads emit a final error frame before closing the stream when a quota/429 is encountered mid-stream; centralize idempotency-key handling and deduplication with a configurable TTL and explicit response behavior; map internal error types to a stable OpenAI-compatible error shape with fields: type, message, param, code to aid SDKs in deterministic behavior.

Behavioral details: - Idempotency: requests with an Idempotency-Key header are recorded in the idempotency store for 24 hours by default (configurable via REDWOOD_IDEMPOTENCY_TTL). If an identical operation (same route + semantic fingerprint) is received while a prior request is pending, the second request will wait up to 30s for the first to complete, then return the original response (200/201/stream) or a 409 if a different side-effect result is observed. Duplicate replays after a completed successful response will return the canonical response and set X-Idempotency-Replayed: true.
- Retry-After & rate limits: 429 responses include Retry-After in seconds and a machine-readable error.code (e.g., rate_limit_exceeded). For streaming, if we hit a global or per-model quota mid-stream we emit a final JSON-chunk matching the OpenAI-compat error shape and close the connection (so clients receive a parseable error).
- Error mapping: internal errors are mapped to OpenAI-compatible error objects (type, message, param, code). Non-user errors include guidance in the message and a recommended action code (e.g., use_smaller_request, backoff).
- Telemetry & observability: added metrics for idempotency store hits/misses, idempotency-replays, rate-limit-trigger counts, and streaming-termination-by-rate-limit. These surface in the Console for per-model/per-route breakdowns.

Files touched are focused and intended to minimize surface risk. The PR includes unit and integration tests that simulate concurrent idempotent requests and forced mid-stream 429s. See commits and changed files below for details.

Related: ENG-4312 (API reliability), ENG-4390 (OpenAI-compat parity).

release_notes:
- Standardize 429 responses to include Retry-After (seconds) and machine-readable error.code.
- Expose consistent X-RateLimit-* headers for streaming and non-streaming endpoints.
- Add configurable idempotency behavior (Idempotency-Key): deduplication, replay markers, and 24h default TTL.
- OpenAI compatibility: stable error shape (type, message, param, code) across runtime.
- Console metrics: idempotency hits/misses and streaming rate-limit terminations.
notes: This change aims to improve SDK compatibility (notably OpenAI-compatible SDKs) and reduce production incidents caused by misinterpreted rate-limit headers. Operators can tune REDWOOD_IDEMPOTENCY_TTL and the pending-wait timeout via config. The in-memory idempotency store is a fallback; for Dedicated and Private deployments we recommend configuring a shared Redis-backed store (implementation hook is provided).
